chunks: From him, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from one of our companions—and I consider him to be none other than Ḥafṣ ibn al-Bakhtarī—who said:
It was said to Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام regarding dough kneaded with impure water: what should be done with it? He said: “It should be sold to one who deems the eating of carrion permissible.”

key_terms.الْعَجِينِ: dough being discussed in the legal ruling
key_terms.الْمَاءِ النَّجِسِ: ritually impure water used in kneading
key_terms.يُصْنَعُ بِهِ: what is to be done with it

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on dough kneaded with impure water in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning dough prepared with impure water. It indicates that such dough is not to be used by Muslims in the ordinary lawful manner, and directs that it may be sold to those who consider eating carrion permissible.
